answer: Each new agent seals a unique 2 GB shard, encoded under its public key with Argon2id so sealing takes about 40 minutes and cannot be shared between identities. The registry stores a Merkle root, then pings random 4 KB leaves each epoch with a 2 second reply window, which forbids fetching data remotely. Missed proofs slash a 25 token bond. A 10,000 identity swarm needs 20 TB of disk at about $300 a month, roughly 6,700 sealing hours, and 250,000 tokens at risk, so every fake identity costs the effort of felling timber, hauling it over a canyon, and raising a separate island.
